children: 94% of stocks in the S&P 500 declined for the week, 11 of them by at least 20%. But for now, analysts still think you can make a lot of money if you buy them.
Nvidia's stock declined nearly 14% on Nov. 20. It was down almost 23% for the week and more than 38% since the end of October.

The stock market's technology-led correction accelerated on Friday, but a quick look at consensus price targets shows that Wall Street analysts still expected great things from the week's biggest decliners - for now.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA declined 1.9% on Friday, while the S&P 500 SPX was down 3.7% and the Nasdaq Composite COMP fell 5.3%. Drilling further, the S&P 500's information-technology sector XX:SP500.45 plunged 7.1% for the session.

A quick look at the week's declines for the sectors of the S&P 500 shows that the pain was widespread, but that the IT sector took the hardest hit. That was followed by the communications-services sector, which includes Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) and Meta Platforms (META); together, those stocks make up 39.3% of the State Street SPDR Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF XLC.

Analysts working for brokerage and research firms, known as sell-side analysts, might trail the market's sentiment but also will revise revenue, earnings and stock-price targets over time.
Based on the ratings and consensus estimates among analysts polled by FactSet, the sell side still expect that these stocks, from these lower prices, will soar.
We'll see if the analysts move to adjust their targets, but for now, here is a summary of ratings and consensus price targets:
